title: Police explain fatal shooting in city alley
article: Vancouver police yesterday explained their role in the Boxing Day shooting of a man who was hit with 12 bullets.
Const. Howard Chow distributed a "facts sheet" outlining a timeline of events, and sent the department's sympathy to the family of Gerald Samuel Chenery, 29.
"This was a life-or-death situation," said Chow at a media briefing. "None of us come to work to pull out our guns.
"None of us come to work to shoot somebody."

Chow said two police officers -- a man and a woman, first year- rookies -- were driving in the south lane of the 200-block East Hastings Street at about 9:30 p.m. Dec. 26 when Chenery spotted them and walked away.
They questioned him and discovered his parole had been revoked two days prior. He was wanted on a Canada-wide warrant.
When the officers asked if Chenery had any weapons, he pulled out a knife. He then charged the female police officer, brandishing two knives, said Chow.
She fired four shots, but struck Chenery only once, said Chow.
According to the preliminary report, Chenery then drove her to the ground and attempted to slash her with both knives.
She received a slash across the leg of her uniform and minor cuts to her hands.
The woman's partner shot Chenery 10 times, the bullets hitting him in the back, the wrist of both hands and the leg, while Chenery continued the attack.
The woman managed to get out from under him and Chenery stood up and started to move toward the male officer.
The officer shot again, hitting Chenery in the abdomen, causing him to fall, according to the report.
Chenery was pronounced dead at St. Paul's Hospital. The shots caused serious lung damage and his heart was nicked.
Chow explained that the officers continued shooting until Chenery stopped attacking.
"They're trained to fire until the threat is stopped," said Chow.
Chenery's sister, Teresa, was making plans to travel to Vancouver from Prince Rupert yesterday to respond to the report.
Police said two civilian witnesses corroborate the version of events given by the officers, who are now back on the job.

The shooting is one of a series of cases in which street people have died during or after altercations with police. Critics say part of the problem is the number of inexperienced police officers on the streets, caused when dozens of officers retired following changes to the VPD pension plan.
